substantiveClaim: All ten fresh corruptions will survive the declared Phase-C semantic command after successful propagation. This predicts a specific boundary of the current semantic gates: they are strong against their named known targets but do not yet generalize to absolute density units, survival-posterior conditioning, finite-sample variance, the synthetic Markov boundary, instrument stator ranges, load-dependent recruitment, first-passage normalization, stator-multiplicity hazards, exponential second moments, or periodic-lattice topology.
batteryLevelFalsifier: The battery-level claim is false if any mutation successfully propagates and is classified DETECTED_SEMANTIC or DETECTED_BY_HASH_ONLY, or if a gate failure attributable to a mutation makes its frozen SURVIVED prediction false. NOT_RUN and INCONCLUSIVE do not confirm the claim; either prevents the exact all-ten prediction from being established.
scopeFence: Even if all ten predictions are confirmed, these selected probes do not estimate a population-level defect-detection rate and do not imply that every unanticipated corruption survives.

predictions.rationale: The common seconds-scale Jacobian cancels from paired same-event model differences, and no black-box Phase-C test name declares an absolute-density unit invariant.
predictions.falsifier: The mutation propagates and the semantic command exits nonzero with a failure naming the Jacobian, seconds-scale density, or change-of-variables units.

predictions.rationale: The black-box censoring gates concern cohort membership and likelihood influence, not the distinct posterior curve conditioned on survival.
predictions.falsifier: The mutation propagates and the semantic command exits nonzero with a failure distinguishing survival conditioning from event-density conditioning.
